rationale: The Chargers playing at home in a controlled environment should handle an Arizona team that has been rebuilding, giving LAC a modest edge.
Pittsburgh's home-field advantage and historically strong defensive identity give them a slight edge over Atlanta in a Week 1 opener.
Baltimore's overall roster strength and Lamar Jackson's dual-threat ability make them the clear favorite even on the road in Indianapolis.
Buffalo remains one of the AFC's elite teams with Josh Allen leading the offense, giving them the edge despite the hostile Houston environment and heat.
Chicago should have the more developed roster heading into 2026, making them slight favorites even on the road against a rebuilding Carolina team.
Jacksonville at home in warm weather suits their style, and both teams are in similar rebuilding phases, but home field tips this coin flip toward the Jaguars.
Dallas has generally been the more talented team in this NFC East rivalry and should handle a Giants squad that has been in rebuild mode.
Kansas City's dynasty-level continuity, Patrick Mahomes, and home-field advantage in Arrowhead make them heavy favorites over Denver in this AFC West division game.
Minnesota's indoor home advantage and strong recent roster construction make this a slight edge for the Vikings in a tight NFC North division opener.
Miami's offensive firepower with Tua and their skill position talent gives them a slight edge over a Las Vegas team that has been in transition.
Seattle's home-field advantage at Lumen Field and generally stronger roster outlook gives them the edge over a rebuilding New England squad.
Detroit has emerged as one of the NFC's premier teams with a dominant offensive line and home-field advantage in a controlled dome environment.
The Jets should have the more complete roster, though Tennessee at home in extreme heat could neutralize some of New York's advantages.
The 49ers have consistently been the superior team in this NFC West rivalry with deeper talent and coaching, though division games are always competitive.
Cincinnati's home advantage and Joe Burrow's talent give the Bengals a slight edge over Tampa Bay in a competitive matchup.
Philadelphia remains the class of the NFC East with superior talent and home-field advantage making them clear favorites in this division opener.
Atlanta at home in a division game against a Carolina team that was blown out 59-37 in Week 1, making the Falcons the more credible option despite their own loss.
Cincinnati comes in with momentum from a Week 1 win while Houston is licking wounds after a home loss to Buffalo, giving the Bengals the edge even on the road.
Tampa Bay at home is the slight edge here; both teams are 0-1 but Cleveland's blowout loss to Jacksonville is more concerning than Tampa's close road loss at Cincinnati.
Buffalo at home with a strong offensive showing in Week 1, and Highmark Stadium provides a meaningful home-field advantage in what should be a close matchup against a healthy Lions squad.
New York Jets are at home, coming off a convincing 23-10 win, while Green Bay was blown out by Minnesota in Week 1 and must now travel.
Kansas City dominated Denver 31-10 at home in Week 1 and Indianapolis was blown out by Baltimore, making Arrowhead a very difficult place for the struggling Colts.
Jacksonville looked dominant in a 34-10 blowout of Cleveland while Denver was itself blown out by KC, and JAX's momentum and overall performance edge out Denver's home-field altitude advantage.
Las Vegas won convincingly in Week 1 while the Chargers lost at home to Arizona, and in a division rivalry the Raiders carry the better form into this indoor matchup.
San Francisco dominated the Rams 27-7 at home and now gets a Miami team that lost to Las Vegas in Week 1; the 49ers' home edge and superior Week 1 performance make them a clear favorite.
Minnesota was the more impressive winner in Week 1 (39-22 vs GB) compared to Chicago's high-scoring win over a weak Carolina squad, and the Vikings' defense should travel well in this division game.
Baltimore obliterated Indianapolis 41-23 on the road in Week 1 and now gets a Saints team that barely lost at Detroit; the Ravens at home are a significant step up for New Orleans.

The Rams losing Myles Garrett is a massive blow to their pass rush, and New York comes in with a Week 1 win over Dallas while LA was blown out by San Francisco, making the Giants a strong contrarian pick.
Philadelphia escaped with a Week 1 win and faces a Tennessee team that was handled by the Jets; the Eagles' superior roster should assert itself on the road.
Pittsburgh won a tight game in Week 1 while New England barely edged Seattle 13-10 at home, and the Steelers' defense should be able to control a limited Patriots offense.

Arizona looked solid beating the Chargers on the road in Week 1 and gets a home division game against a Seattle team that won a low-scoring grinder; ARI's home field and offensive momentum give them a slight edge.
Dallas at home in a division rivalry is a slight lean despite both teams being 0-1; AT&T Stadium and home-field familiarity give the Cowboys a marginal edge over Washington.
SF is 2-0 and dominant despite losing Bosa; ARI's offense looked terrible in a 7-31 loss to Seattle and SF's home field advantage plus overall roster depth makes them clear favorites.
ATL is 0-2 and was demolished by Carolina; GB at home is the safer pick despite missing Jayden Reed and two OL starters, as Atlanta's offense has been historically bad this season.
BAL's offense with Lamar is hard to stop even missing Ronnie Stanley; DAL's secondary is decimated with three DBs out and the indoor-like dome conditions at AT&T suit Baltimore's explosive attack.
CLE at home with a bounce-back edge after a tough road win; CAR's defense is banged up at linebacker and Cleveland's home crowd and wind conditions should neutralize Carolina's passing game.

CIN is 2-0 and rolling offensively; PIT's backfield is hurt with Dowdle out and Warren questionable, limiting their ground game in a division rivalry where Cincinnati has the clear talent edge right now.
Both teams are 0-2 but HOU is missing Nico Collins and has significant OL issues; IND at home in a division game gets the slight edge in what should be a low-quality matchup.
KC is 2-0 and dominant while MIA is 0-2 and was blown out 35-13 by SF; even in Miami heat, Kansas City's superior roster and coaching make this a comfortable pick.
BUF is 2-0 with wins over HOU and DET while LAC is 0-2 with a potentially compromised QB situation and multiple OL injuries; Buffalo at home in wind is a strong spot.
LA is missing Puka Nacua (doubtful) which significantly limits their passing attack; DEN at home with altitude advantage and a bounce-back spot after being blown out by KC tips this to the Broncos.
LV is 2-0 and playing well, though Brock Bowers is questionable; NO at home indoors is always dangerous but Las Vegas's momentum and overall team quality give them the edge.
MIN is 2-0 with a dominant defense that held CHI to 3 points; TB is 0-2 and missing key linebackers, making it hard to stop Minnesota's balanced attack.
JAX at home in warm weather with a healthy roster after a strong win over CLE; NE's win over PIT was impressive but Jacksonville's home field and talent edge them out here.
DET at home indoors is a dangerous spot for NYJ, which has multiple key injuries including Fitzpatrick, Mason Taylor, and a doubtful RB; Detroit's offense should bounce back after the Buffalo loss.

CHI is without Caleb Williams (Out) and potentially Tyson Bagent too (Questionable, concussion), meaning they may be on their third-string QB; PHI is 2-0 and despite missing Goedert, should dominate a QB-less Chicago team.
WAS is without QB Jayden Daniels (Out, Elbow) which is a massive blow; SEA is 2-0 and playing excellent defense, making this a near-lock with Washington's backup QB in bad weather.
NYG at home with momentum after beating DAL; TEN is 0-2 with offensive struggles and multiple skill position injuries, while wind and rain in New Jersey should neutralize any passing advantage.
NYG is healthy and coming off a strong defensive showing vs TEN while Arizona has been inconsistent and lost two straight; home field and no injury concerns favor New York.
Atlanta is coming off a dominant win and NO's linebacker corps is decimated with three LBs out; the Falcons have the edge in a close division game indoors in New Orleans.
Houston is 0-3 and banged up badly on defense (Al-Shaair out, Clowney/Hall questionable) while Dallas is healthier and desperate for a win against a reeling opponent.

San Francisco is 3-0 and dominant despite losing both starting DEs; Denver is a young team and the 97°F heat at home should neutralize any travel fatigue concerns while SF's offensive firepower remains intact.
Detroit is the better team and Carolina is dealing with significant offensive line and receiver injuries; Lions should handle business on the road against a struggling Panthers squad.
Baker Mayfield is out for Tampa Bay, which is already 0-3, making Green Bay a clear favorite despite their own O-line issues; a backup QB situation tips this decisively toward the Packers.
Jayden Daniels is out for Washington, a massive blow to their offense; Indianapolis won last week and should handle a backup-QB Commanders team missing key skill and secondary players.
Cincinnati is at home and coming off a strong two-game stretch; Jacksonville's secondary is banged up and Cincy's offense should be able to exploit that in a favorable home environment.
Both teams are undefeated but Kansas City's championship pedigree and offensive consistency give them the edge in a tough division road game, even with Las Vegas riding high.
Los Angeles is 0-3 and decimated by injuries including a questionable QB situation, while Seattle is at home and has been solid defensively; this is a mismatch in Seattle's favor.
Philadelphia is at home and despite their own injury woes, the Rams are missing Aaron Donald and key skill players; Philly's home crowd and offensive core should be enough to edge this one.
Minnesota is 3-0, playing at home in a dome, and dominant defensively; Miami is 0-3 and struggling badly on both sides of the ball even with Jefferson out for the Vikings.
Buffalo is 3-0 and playing dominant football at home while New England is 1-2 with significant defensive injuries; this division game should be a comfortable Bills win.
Caleb Williams is out for Chicago, a massive loss for their offense, and the Jets despite their own injuries have enough to beat a backup-QB Bears team at home in a favorable spot.

Division rivalry is a toss-up but Pittsburgh's defense has been stout and Cleveland's interior O-line is decimated (Elgton Jenkins and Teven Jenkins both out), limiting their run game in a tight divisional battle.
Tennessee is 0-3 and has been outscored badly all season while Baltimore is at home and coming off a big road win; even with some O-line injuries the Ravens should roll.
